**Proof.**

By the argument principle, since $f$ is holomorphic in a neighborhood of $\overline{D(0,R)}$ and has no zeros on $\partial D(0,R)$, the number of zeros (counted with multiplicity) in $D(0,R)$ is

$$
N = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z|=R} \frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,dz.
$$

Parametrize the circle by $z = Re^{i\theta}$, $\theta\in[0,2\pi]$, so $dz = iRe^{i\theta}\,d\theta = iz\,d\theta$. Substituting,

$$
N = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_0^{2\pi} \frac{f'(Re^{i\theta})}{f(Re^{i\theta})}\cdot iRe^{i\theta}\,d\theta = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} z\frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,d\theta,
$$

where $z = Re^{i\theta}$ throughout the integrand. Since $N$ is a nonnegative integer (hence real), taking real parts of both sides yields

$$
N = \operatorname{Re}(N) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\operatorname{Re}\!\left(z\frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\right)d\theta.
$$

Thus $N$ equals the average value of the continuous function $g(\theta) := \operatorname{Re}\!\left(z\frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\right)\Big|_{z=Re^{i\theta}}$ on $[0,2\pi]$. (Continuity holds because $f$ has no zeros on $|z|=R$, so $f'/f$ is continuous there.)

The maximum of a continuous function on a compact set is at least its average:

$$
\max_{|z|=R}\operatorname{Re}\!\left(z\frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\right) = \max_{\theta\in[0,2\pi]} g(\theta) \;\geq\; \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} g(\theta)\,d\theta = N.
$$

Therefore

$$
\max_{|z|=R}\operatorname{Re}\!\left(z\frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\right) \geq N. \qquad\blacksquare
$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
